question: During the Basic Control Skills test, what is scored as a 'pull-up'?
choice_a: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_b: Backing up on a forward moving exercise to clear an encroachment
choice_c: Crossing over an exercise boundary line with any part of the vehicle
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check its position during a backing exercise
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward on a backing exercise (Exercise 2 and Exercise 4) to clear an encroachment or to get a better position; stopping without changing direction does not count.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-1

question: On Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, what is scored as a 'back-up'?
choice_a: Crossing a boundary line with the vehicle's mirror
choice_b: Backing up on a forward moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_c: Pulling forward to clear an encroachment
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
explanation: The manual states that backing up on a forward moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position is scored as a 'back-up,' and this is scored specifically on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-1

question: What is scored as an 'encroachment' during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Stopping without changing direction
choice_b: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
choice_c: Crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors
choice_d: Sounding the horn before completing an exercise
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as crossing over or touching exercise boundary lines or cones with any portion of the vehicle other than the mirrors (or unique vehicle parts below door mirror height).
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-1

question: Before exiting the vehicle to check its position during a backing exercise, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Turn off the engine completely
choice_b: Set the parking brake and place the vehicle in neutral
choice_c: Activate the four-way flashers
choice_d: Sound the horn twice
explanation: The manual requires the driver to set the parking brake and place the vehicle in neutral before safely exiting/entering the vehicle, facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-1

topic: Unsafe Act - Opening Door While Moving
question: What happens if a driver opens the vehicle door while it is moving (not in neutral and park) during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: A one-point deduction is applied
choice_b: It counts only as a 'look'
choice_c: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_d: The examiner issues a warning and the exercise restarts
explanation: The manual states that if the driver opens the door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-2

question: How many free looks (exits to check vehicle position) are allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, respectively?
choice_a: Two free looks on Exercise 2 and one free look on Exercise 4
choice_b: One free look on Exercise 2 and two free looks on Exercise 4
choice_c: Zero free looks on either exercise
choice_d: Three free looks on each exercise
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and two free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, to check the position of the vehicle.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-2

question: Final vehicle position is scored on which two Basic Control Skills exercises?
choice_a: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
choice_b: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_c: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_d: All four exercises equally
explanation: The manual states final vehicle position is scored on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-2

question: During Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, how many times may the driver stop the vehicle?
choice_a: As many times as needed to align correctly
choice_b: Only once
choice_c: Up to two times
choice_d: Unlimited, as long as final position is correct
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to drive forward through the alley and stop with the front most part of the vehicle within the box, noting the driver may stop only once.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-2

question: On Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, the driver is scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and final position, and is allowed how many free pull-ups?
choice_a: Zero free pull-ups
choice_b: One free pull-up
choice_c: Two free pull-ups
choice_d: Three free pull-ups
explanation: The manual states that for Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, the driver is scored for pull-ups, encroachments and final position, and is allowed one free pull-up and may exit the vehicle only one time to check around it.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-3

question: On Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, how many free back-ups are allowed and may the driver exit the vehicle during the exercise?
choice_a: One free back-up is allowed, and the driver may exit once
choice_b: There are no free back-ups, and the driver is not permitted to exit the vehicle
choice_c: Two free back-ups are allowed, and the driver may exit twice
choice_d: Free back-ups are unlimited, but exiting is prohibited
explanation: The manual states there are NO free back-ups on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and the driver is NOT permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-3

topic: Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing Final Position
question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, the rear most part of the vehicle must stop within how many feet of the rear of the alley?
choice_a: One (1) foot
choice_b: Three (3) feet
choice_c: Five (5) feet
choice_d: Ten (10) feet
explanation: The manual requires the driver to offset back into the alley, bringing the rear most part of the vehicle within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley and stopping in the three-foot box at the end of the alley.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-3

question: On Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, how many free pull-ups are allowed and how many times may the driver exit the vehicle to check around it?
choice_a: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_b: Two free pull-ups and two exits
choice_c: Zero free pull-ups and one exit
choice_d: Three free pull-ups and three exits
explanation: The manual states the driver is allowed two free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around it during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 12-3

question: If stopping behind another vehicle on the road test, where should the driver stop to maintain a safe gap?
choice_a: Close enough to touch the vehicle's rear bumper
choice_b: Where the driver can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead
choice_c: At least three car lengths back regardless of visibility
choice_d: Wherever traffic allows, since gap distance is not scored
explanation: The manual instructs that if stopping behind another vehicle, the driver should stop where they can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of them, which represents a safe gap.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-1

question: When required to stop at an intersection during the road test, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Coast to a stop to save fuel
choice_b: Come to a complete stop with no coasting, and the vehicle must not roll forward or backward
choice_c: Stop only if a police officer is present
choice_d: Roll slowly through if no cross traffic is visible
explanation: The manual requires the driver to come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind stop signs, signals, or stop lines, and states the vehicle must not roll forward or backward.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-1

question: During the urban business portion of the road test, where should the vehicle be positioned and how should speed be managed?
choice_a: Centered in the left-most lane, driving as fast as safely possible
choice_b: Centered in the proper (right-most) lane, keeping up with traffic flow but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_c: Straddling two lanes to allow for turns
choice_d: In any lane, since urban business driving is not scored
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and the driver should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-2

question: Before changing lanes during the multiple-lane portion of the road test, what must the driver do first?
choice_a: Activate the four-way flashers
choice_b: Make the necessary traffic checks, then use proper signals and change lanes when safe
choice_c: Signal and change lanes immediately without checking traffic
choice_d: Slow to a stop before changing lanes
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-2

question: Before entering the expressway during the road test, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic
choice_b: Come to a complete stop at the on-ramp
choice_c: Activate four-way flashers before merging
choice_d: Merge at the posted speed limit regardless of traffic gaps
explanation: The manual states that before entering the expressway, the driver must check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-2

question: For the Stop/Start maneuver, after bringing the vehicle to a full stop as if to check something on it, what must the driver do once stopped?
choice_a: Leave the vehicle in drive with a foot on the brake
choice_b: Activate four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and move the gear shift to neutral or park
choice_c: Immediately exit the vehicle without securing it
choice_d: Turn off the engine and remove the key
explanation: The manual states that once stopped for the Stop/Start maneuver, the driver must activate the four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and move the gear shift to neutral or park.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-2

question: When approaching a curve during the road test, what should the driver do before entering the curve?
choice_a: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_b: Reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_c: Shift to neutral to coast through the curve
choice_d: Brake hard at the apex of the curve
explanation: The manual instructs that before entering a curve, the driver should reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required while in the curve.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-2

question: While any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing, what is the driver prohibited from doing?
choice_a: Keeping both hands on the steering wheel
choice_b: Checking traffic in all directions
choice_c: Stopping, changing gears, passing another vehicle, or changing lanes
choice_d: Maintaining a steady speed across the tracks
explanation: The manual states that drivers must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-2

topic: Railroad Crossing - Bus and Placarded Vehicles
question: A driver of a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards must stop within how many feet of, but not less than how many feet from, the nearest rail at a railroad crossing (unless exempt)?
choice_a: Within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet
choice_b: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
choice_c: Within 25 feet but not less than 5 feet
choice_d: Within 15 feet but not less than 5 feet
explanation: The manual states such drivers must stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail, then look and listen for an approaching train.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-3

question: After driving under an overpass or over a bridge during the road test, what might the examiner ask the driver to identify?
choice_a: The color of the overpass structure
choice_b: The posted clearance or height (for an overpass) and the posted weight limit (for a bridge)
choice_c: The name of the engineering firm that built the bridge
choice_d: The number of support columns under the overpass
explanation: The manual states that after driving under an overpass, the driver may be asked the posted clearance or height, and after going over a bridge, the posted weight limit.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-3

question: If a driver is operating a vehicle with an unsynchronized manual transmission during the road test, what technique must be used when shifting?
choice_a: Single-clutching only
choice_b: Double-clutching
choice_c: Riding the clutch to control speed
choice_d: Popping the clutch quickly between gears
explanation: The manual states that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, the driver must double-clutch when shifting, and must not rev or lug the engine.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-3

question: According to the general driving behavior rules for lane usage, where should a driver finish a left turn on a multiple-lane road, and where should a right turn finish?
choice_a: A left turn finishes in the lane directly to the right of the center line; a right turn finishes in the right-most (curb) lane
choice_b: Both turns must finish in the left-most lane
choice_c: A left turn finishes in the curb lane; a right turn finishes in the center lane
choice_d: Lane finishing position is not scored during turns
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line on a multiple lane road, and finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 13-4
